clue.text: Moving up?

definitions.meaning: under way, as a project that has started

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, 'Moving up?' looks like a promotion; split, it gives under way and literally airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a venture that is properly started is said to have left the earth, like a plane taking off.

clue.text: Busy part of month, e.g. October

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone says that a stretch of a month such as October is a hectic time.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person constantly active and rushing about is described with this phrase, meaning occupied.

clue.text: Flying boats

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: an adjective for swift and a noun for a group of ships sailing together.

clue.text: An order to run railway over part of bridge

parts.note: hie is an old word meaning to hasten or hurry

indicators.note: over here means placed around, so the railway letters sit on either side of the bridge part

parts.note: an arch is the curved span of a bridge

explanation.surface: An instruction is given to lay a railway line across a section of a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means around rather than signalling a reversal, and HIE is an archaic verb for hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarchy is a ranked system, an order of precedence in which each level sits above the next.

clue.text: Good argument for progress

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A sound debate is recommended as a way of moving things forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to develop or advance is to increase in size or maturity.

clue.text: Newspaper has to pass on material

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or journal, especially one speaking for a party or group
to pass on is a euphemism for to die

explanation.surface: A newspaper is obliged to forward some material to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass on' looks like handing something over, but it is the euphemism for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff, translucent cotton fabric, so it is an example of a material.

clue.text: All Time Low in North America, free to return

indicators.note: to return means the word for free comes back on itself, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of pests

explanation.surface: All Time Low, the American pop-punk band, are in North America and free to come home.
explanation.walkthrough: All Time Low is the name of a US rock band, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the nadir is the lowest point ever reached, the very bottom of a decline.

clue.text: Officer material

definitions.meaning: a non-commissioned army rank above lance ...
bodily, physical, as opposed to spiritual

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone suitable for promotion, 'officer material'; read apart, it is a rank and an adjective meaning physical.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an NCO rank in the army, and an adjective meaning of the body rather than the spirit.

clue.text: Word — plural form of butt

parts.note: PL is the grammar abbreviation for plural
a butt is an end or border, and to butt is to abut, so edge is a form of the idea

explanation.surface: A grammar note declares the plural of 'butt' to be a certain word.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a grammar lesson, but 'plural' only gives PL and 'form of butt' is a synonym for edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: giving your word means making a solemn promise, which is a vow or undertaking.

clue.text: Air show has them for one hugging boy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: hugging means the two letters for example wrap around the word for boy

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'for one' means
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: An aerial display includes a group of performers embracing a young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air show' reads as an aerobatic display, but it is a tune (air) belonging to a programme (show).
explanation.definitionFit: The signature tune of a television programme or film is the melody identified with that production.

clue.text: Funny Girl's conclusion, my turn

indicators.note: turn means the exclamation word is flipped to read the other way round

parts.note: My Lord! is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

indicators.note: a conclusion is the end, so the last letter of the word girl is taken

explanation.surface: It looks like a reference to the musical Funny Girl ending, followed by a player saying it is their go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny Girl' looks like the musical's title; 'Funny' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: drily amusing or quaintly comic, a wry kind of humour.

clue.text: Deceive other half over missing recipe

indicators.note: over means the shortened word is turned around and read from the end
missing means the abbreviation for recipe is dropped from the word for spouse

parts.note: one's other half is a spouse or partner
R is the abbreviation for recipe (take), as on old prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone tricks their spouse after a recipe has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes R from PARTNER, leaving PARTNE, which 'over' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to snare or trick someone into a compromising position is to mislead them.

clue.text: Hardy's anger about books reflecting decline

indicators.note: about means the word for anger goes around the Testament abbreviation

parts.note: ire is anger
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: reflecting means the word for fall appears as in a mirror, back to front

parts.note: a dip is a decline or fall

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy's rage about novels that show a falling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' suggests the novelist Thomas Hardy, but it is the adjective, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hardy in the sense of bold and fearless, undaunted by danger.

clue.text: Bad murder charge

parts.note: food that has gone off is bad
to ice someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: A wrongful accusation of homicide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'murder charge' looks like a legal accusation; 'charge' is a duty or post.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a charge in the sense of a duty or position of responsibility, like the office of mayor.

clue.text: About to enter side of Nottingham that's divine

indicators.note: to enter means the abbreviation for about goes inside the name of the team

parts.note: Nottingham Forest is a football team, a side, from the English city of Nottingham
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Something is about to get into Nottingham's team, which is described as heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: NOTTINGHAM FOREST is an English football club. 'divine' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to divine is to predict what is coming, as a prophet or weather presenter does.

clue.text: Scatter food, not hot as such

indicators.note: not means the abbreviation for hot is left out of the word for food

parts.note: a dish is a prepared item of food
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
per se is Latin for in itself, as such

explanation.surface: A cook is told to spread food around without heating it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to scatter a crowd is to break it up and send people off in different directions.

clue.text: Almost give Bond's location

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for slack is dropped

parts.note: a rope or a floor has play or give when it yields slightly
cement bonds things together

explanation.surface: Someone nearly reveals where James Bond is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests James Bond, but it is cement; 'give' is a noun, slack.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a placement is a position or site where something is put.

clue.text: A humming insect

parts.note: humming here is British slang for smelling bad, not buzzing; this bug gives off a foul odour

explanation.walkthrough: Humming suggests buzzing wings, but in British slang to hum is to stink, which describes this shield bug that releases a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a shield bug that releases a foul odour when disturbed is literally a smelly bug.

clue.text: Plymouth Brethren member's brave to keep next to it

indicators.note: to keep means the word for face boldly holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to brave or dare is to face boldly
by means beside or next to
taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchman summons up courage to keep something close beside him.
explanation.walkthrough: The Plymouth Brethren are a Christian group; their founder John Nelson Darby gave this follower's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a follower of John Nelson Darby, founder of the Exclusive branch of the Plymouth Brethren.

clue.text: Attorney about to work against the law

indicators.note: about means the prosecutor abbreviation goes around the word for damage

parts.note: DA, district attorney, is an American prosecutor
to harm is to damage or work against

explanation.surface: A lawyer is about to act in opposition to the law.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist teaching, dharma is the cosmic law and moral order governing conduct.

clue.text: Beer with a straw? One might be sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the word for a vote is placed in reverse order

parts.note: a straw poll is an informal vote, so a poll might be straw

explanation.surface: A drink served with a straw might be sent back to the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: WALLOP is British slang for beer. 'straw? One might be' points to a straw poll, so POLL reversed gives LLOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: in Britain, a pint of ale is jokingly called this, a word otherwise meaning a heavy blow.

clue.text: Canoe is very good out of control

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is slang for very good or sanctimonious
a rogue elephant or trader is out of control

explanation.surface: A boat is said to be excellent though it runs wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pirogue is a long narrow dugout canoe, used in Louisiana and the Caribbean.

clue.text: Only wants to capture top gangster

indicators.note: wants to capture means the word for only surrounds the word for lid

parts.note: alone means only, as in he alone knew
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: A single-minded crook just wants to seize the leading criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Scarface, the Chicago mobster of the Prohibition era, is the most famous American gangster.

clue.text: Hidden delta in South American country

indicators.note: in means the phonetic letter goes inside the country name

parts.note: Peru is a country in South America
D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A river delta lies concealed in a South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdu is French for lost, used in English to mean concealed, out of sight.

clue.text: German city putting one million into sport

indicators.note: putting with into means placing the numeral and abbreviation within the word for show off
into completes the instruction begun by putting: the numeral and abbreviation go inside the word for show off

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A German city invests a million in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' is the verb, to show off clothes, not athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Weimar is a city in Thuringia, home of Goethe and of the post-war republic's constitution.

clue.text: I wound up in US city

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to maim is to wound

explanation.surface: Someone ended up in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' reads as ended up; split, it is MAIM plus a reversal, so 'up' turns IMAIM around.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Miami is a city on the coast of Florida in the United States.

clue.text: While talking, drag pig

indicators.note: while talking means the word for tedious thing is heard as speech, giving a similar spelling

parts.note: a drag is something tedious, a bore

explanation.surface: Someone drags a pig along while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a boar is a male pig or a wild pig.

clue.text: Man with no time to be a hoarder

indicators.note: with no means the abbreviation for time is taken out of the form of address

parts.note: mister is a form of address for a man

explanation.surface: A man without spare time ends up hoarding things.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a skinflint who stockpiles money and will not spend it.

clue.text: Get off me, chimed Kylie?

definitions.note: kylie is an Aboriginal Australian word for this curved throwing stick

parts.note: boo is what a crowd shouts to tell a performer to get off
taken as written
rang is chimed, as a bell

explanation.surface: Kylie Minogue sings out 'get off me'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kylie' suggests Kylie Minogue, but a kylie is an Australian throwing stick; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A kylie is an Aboriginal throwing stick, a curved wooden weapon that flies back to the thrower.

clue.text: Fast way to attract attention

parts.note: fast here means going without food, not quick: refusing to eat as a protest draws public notice

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast way' suggests a quick method; the fast is abstinence from food, used as protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a prisoner or activist refuses all food as a protest to force public notice of a cause.
